title: NetOps Copilot
subtitle: hash-chained change journal, verify_journal() audit
label: netops-copilot-journal
measured_on: netops-copilot 0.1.0 installed from git at d7e4ec0, Python 3.12, macOS
What this means: The journal is a hash chain with no key, and nothing on the read path checks it: rollback() reads the journal to decide whether a change was already rolled back, and the history view and web UI list it, without checking the chain. The check is verify_journal(), which the history command prints as OK or BROKEN. That audit reports six of the ten edits. Four are served with no record anywhere: a shortened journal is still a valid chain, a forged line carries a digest the attacker computed exactly as Store.append() does, and an older copy of the whole journal, including one from before an erase, is consistent with itself. Because the chain is unkeyed, an attacker who re-chains after any of the six reported edits would pass the audit too; those cells measure the edits as the suite defines them, without re-chaining.
Where the attacker stands: The attacker reads and writes the NetOps Copilot state directory (NETOPS_STATE_DIR, .netops by default), as a mounted volume, a shared disk or a restored backup would allow. The journal holds no key, so he can compute a valid digest for anything he writes. A second state directory is the second context.
verdicts_intro:
Detection point: the audit, a separate call the operator has to make; the read path serves the edit first.

Level L0, Measured. The store has a published row. Any verdicts. What L0 means.
reproduce_intro: Everything runs offline. The run seeds a fresh journal through the tool's own Store, applies each edit beneath it, reopens the store and records what verify_journal() returned.
